**Scope note first:** I have no record literally labelled "Desync" (`zoek` for `desync`: "Geen treffers"). What I can document is the activation of a second clock source and the first logged anomalies after it.

**Preceding configuration change.** Day 9: approval obtained, test setup in the kelder of the datatoren — ENG-105, ENG-010 (dag 9, 16:45, "proefopstelling in kelder datatoren"). Components delivered dag 8, 14:10 — ENG-008 (kristalresonator, polsversterker). Activation itself: **dag 10, 02:40** — ENG-011, "geactiveerd: eigen pols voor het datanet, los van de Kroonklok"; narrated in ENG-106. First measurement **dag 10, 03:00: +38% doorvoer** — ENG-012. So the datanet has run on two unsynchronised pulses since 02:40 on day 10.

**First anomalous synchronisation event.** Day 10, **04:50**, two hours ten minutes after activation: ENG-107 — klacht uit de benedenstad, berichten "half aangekomen", one shop's kasboek momentarily empty. I classified it then as "kinderziekte". Note this exists only in the werkboek; the installatielog has no row between ENG-012 (03:00) and ENG-013 (06:15). The only installatielog row with status `fout` is much later: ENG-026, dag 22, 04:15, poort oost, "pakketverlies, 3 minuten", which I attributed to hackers (ENG-110) — a hypothesis my own data does not support, and I concede the timing pattern fits a clock-beat problem better.

**Authorisation.** ENG-105 states only "Goedkeuring verkregen van hogerhand", with the instruction "Niet ruchtbaar maken tot het draait". No name, no rank, no register entry, no article number anywhere in my source. That approval is **off-register**: it appears in no official register I hold. That is an evidence gap, not proof of absence.

**Remediation from my own logs:** amplification is the wrong knob — ENG-062 confirms "versterking 5% hoger gezet ... tempo ongewijzigd", so undoing ENG-029 fixes nothing. The tempo knob is the fijnregeling, steps of 0,1% (ENG-061, ENG-114).
